summary:
Project Viber, developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, introduces "Earth Pulse," an innovative web application that bridges the gap between complex Earth science and public accessibility. While NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) provides stunning visual data of our changing planet, visualization alone can limit broader audience reach. Earth Pulse solves this challenge by transforming scientific data into a multi-sensory experience through real-time sonification.
The application pairs EIC visual frames with dynamic musical instruments: forests (NDVI) are represented by lead guitar, ocean temperatures (SST) by bass guitar, global temperature anomalies by piano, atmospheric cloud cover by clarinet, and ice sheet mass loss by drums. Users can explore this interactive space-themed interface in ensemble mode or isolate individual instrument channels through a solo feature. By converting satellite observations into sound, Earth Pulse makes global climate science engaging, emotional, and accessible to everyone.
details:
Project Name: Earth Pulse (Project Viber)

Challenge: The Earth Information Jukebox

Summary:

NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) produces stunning visual data of our changing planet; however, presenting complex Earth science through visualization alone limits accessibility for broader audiences. To bridge this gap, we developed Earth Pulse, an innovative, multi-sensory web application that translates NASA’s Earth observation data into dynamic musical sonifications in real time.

Key Features & Data Mapping:

Madde işareti Forests (NDVI): Mapped to Lead Guitar to reflect vegetative health and ecosystem vitality [+2.4%].

Madde işareti Ocean Temperatures (SST): Mapped to Bass Guitar to represent marine thermal shifts [+0.8°C].

Madde işareti Global Temperature Anomalies: Mapped to Piano to sonify climate deviations [+1.3°C].

Madde işareti Atmospheric Cloud Cover: Mapped to Clarinet to capture dynamic atmospheric coverage [+5.1%].

Madde işareti Ice Sheet Mass Loss: Mapped to Drums to emphasize critical cryosphere decline [-286 Gt].

Functionality & User Experience:

Built with a futuristic NASA-inspired UI, Earth Pulse features an interactive rotating globe and a dual-mode audio engine. Users can experience the global data symphony in Ensemble Mode or isolate individual channels using the Solo Feature. By blending science with art, Earth Pulse makes global climate monitoring engaging, emotional, and universally accessible.
